faqs.question: A label peeled off in the product. How should I remove it?
faqs.answer:
Press the product's
LF/FF
button until the label appears on the platen and remove the label. If you can't remove the label this way, do not remove the platen from the product. Get the printer serviced.
Note:
We recommend you use the pull tractor to print labels. Labels fed through the rear push tractor can curl and peel off under the platen.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

See our

faqs.question: When I print on single sheets, the first page prints correctly, but the print on the following pages starts too low on the page. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure you have single sheet (or cut-sheet) selected as the paper type in the printer driver. If you're using non-Windows software, check if the software has a lines per page setting and set it to 61 lines per page.

faqs.question: How do I create a custom paper size in the Server Properties?
faqs.answer:
Follow these steps to create a new page size accessible by all printer drivers installed in Windows:
Open the
Printers
or
Printers and Faxes
window.
Click
File
, then
Server Properties
.
Put a check in the
Create a new form
box.
Input a name for the custom paper size.
Under
Paper Size
, enter the desired height and width.
Click
Save
or
Save Form
to add the new form size to the list, then
OK
to close Server Properties.

faqs.question: Can I use the platen knob to load or adjust paper?
faqs.answer:
No. Use the Load/Eject button to load or remove paper and the micro adjust feature to
adjust the top-of-form position
. The knob should only be used to clear paper jams after the printer has been turned off.

faqs.question: My product will not print through a PC serial connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure you're using a null modem cable.
Make sure the serial connection settings on the printer matches the settings on your computer. See
Changing the Printer's Default Settings
to change the printer's settings.
Make sure the cable connection is not loose.
Try a different cable.

faqs.question: Can I print on checks that are 3-inches in length?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You'll need to set up the paper size in your software. In Windows you'll need to define a custom paper size. If you're using software that does not have an option to set a paper size, try setting the page size on the printer. See
Changing the Default Settings
in the
LX-300+II Reference Guide
.
Note: Software settings always override the printer's default settings.

faqs.answer:
Set the printer's character table to PC 437. See
Changing the Printer's Default Settings
.

faqs.question: Are dip switches used to change settings on my product?
faqs.answer:
No. The printer has built-in default settings. You can change the settings using the printer's front panel buttons. For more information, see
Changing the Printer's Default Settings
.

faqs.question: Can my product emulate an IBM Proprinter?
faqs.answer: Yes. The printer emulates the IBM 2380 Plus.

faqs.question: Does my product support an IBM mainframe (IBM 3270) or IBM minicomputer (AS/400 or System 3X) environment?
faqs.answer: No. The printer does not have the optional slot necessary to connect to a mainframe or minicomputer system.

faqs.question: What is the recommended duty cycle for my product?
faqs.answer: The recommended duty cycle is 25 percent. This describes the printer's condition when it is printing (not idle) for 2 hours a day, 22 days per month.

faqs.question: My product does not load paper to the correct top-of-form position. How can I change the position?
faqs.answer:
Use the printer's micro adjust feature to adjust the position. See
Adjusting the top-of-form position
for more information.
Caution:
Never use the knob to adjust the top-of-form position; this may damage the printer or cause it to lose the top-of-form position.

faqs.question: My product intermittently looses data with a serial connection set to a 9600 baud rate or higher. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Use a DTR setting if you can. If you must use XON/XOFF, decrease the baud rate. (At 9600 the XOFF signal may not reach the printer in time to delay data transmission and this will result in a loss of data.)

faqs.question: Does my product print landscape fonts?
faqs.answer: The printer does not include landscape fonts as part of its built-in character set. If you're printing from Windows, however, it can print TrueType fonts in landscape.

faqs.question: Why does my product stop or pause in the middle of a large print job?
faqs.answer: The printer will pause or stop if it's waiting for more data or processing data received from a computer. It may also pause or slow down to ensure the print head does not overheat. It resumes printing once the print head has cooled down.
